dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef001 representable exact rounded means that rounded is representable and, for every representable real candidate, |exact - rounded| ≤ |exact - candidate|. Thus rounded is a globally nearest representable real to exact in absolute error, with ties allowed.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied with exact = x + y and rounded = s, it states that s is representable and minimizes absolute error from x + y among all representable reals. Since x is representable, choosing candidate = x gives |(x + y) - s| ≤ |(x + y) - x| = |y|, equivalent to the target inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: HAdd.hAdd extracts and applies the binary addition-like operation supplied by an HAdd instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the Real addition instance supplied through instHAdd, every occurrence denotes ordinary real addition, particularly x + y.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: HSub.hSub extracts and applies the binary subtraction-like operation supplied by an HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the Real subtraction instance supplied through instHSub, it forms the real differences s - (x + y), (x + y) - s, and (x + y) - candidate.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: LE.le extracts the non-strict comparison relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With Real.instLE, it makes both the nearest-representable condition and the conclusion non-strict inequalities over real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The variables x, y, and s, all candidates, and all exact and error quantities are scalar real numbers; no vector or matrix dimensions occur.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAdd equips the real numbers with their real addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines x + y and also supplies the addition used in the definition of real subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAddGroup supplies the additive-group structure on the real numbers, including zero, addition, and additive negation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides the negation required by absolute value and supports the standard identities used to read subtraction and simplify (x + y) - x to y.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instLE equips the real numbers with their standard less-than-or-equal relation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the conclusion as |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y| and interprets the minimization comparison inside LocalDef001.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instSub defines real subtraction by a - b = a + (-b).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the exact meanings of all error differences, including s - (x + y) and exact - candidate.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.lattice supplies the lattice structure on the real numbers, including the maximum operation compatible with the real order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the maximum operation used to define absolute value as max(a, -a).

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an element a of a lattice-ordered additive group, abs a is defined as max(a, -a); over the reals this is the usual absolute value |a|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It measures scalar absolute error. The target compares the absolute error of s as an approximation to x + y with |y|.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHAdd converts a homogeneous Add instance into an HAdd instance by forwarding hAdd directly to the supplied addition operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instAdd, it ensures that the elaborated HAdd expression applied to x and y is ordinary real addition x + y.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHSub converts a homogeneous Sub instance into an HSub instance by forwarding hSub directly to the supplied subtraction operation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instSub, it ensures that all elaborated HSub expressions are ordinary real subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: And is logical conjunction: And P Q holds exactly when both P and Q hold.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Inside LocalDef001 it requires both that s is representable and that s satisfies the nearest-representable error inequality against every representable candidate.

binders: representable is an arbitrary predicate on the real numbers, equivalently an arbitrary subset of the reals.
x, y, and s are arbitrary scalar real numbers.
hypotheses: For every real candidate c, if c is representable, then |(x + y) - s| ≤ |(x + y) - c|; that is, s is a nearest representable real to the exact real number x + y.
conclusions: The absolute error of s relative to x + y satisfies |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|.
mathematical_definitions: The exact quantity being approximated is the real sum x + y.
Nearest representable means minimizing absolute error over every real satisfying the predicate representable; minimizers need not be unique.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every subset of the real numbers designated as representable and all real numbers x, y, and s, if x is representable and s is a representable real nearest to the exact sum x + y in absolute error, then |s - (x + y)| ≤ |y|. The result follows because x itself is an admissible representable candidate, whose distance from x + y is exactly |y|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The predicate representable is completely arbitrary; the proposition encodes no floating-point format, precision, exponent range, spacing, closure property, or finiteness condition.
Only x and s are required to be representable. Neither y nor the exact sum x + y is required to be representable.
The hypothesis on s is a global nearest-point condition over all representable reals, not merely a local condition despite the definition's name.
Ties are allowed because the minimizing comparison uses ≤; uniqueness of s is not asserted.
All quantities are scalar real numbers, and the error measure is ordinary absolute value rather than a vector or matrix norm.
The addition x + y and all error computations are exact real arithmetic; no intermediate rounding, overflow, underflow, exceptional values, or relative-error interpretation is encoded.
For choices of x, y, and s where either x is not representable or s does not satisfy the nearest-representable condition, the implication is true vacuously.
When the hypotheses hold, representable cannot be empty because both x and s are representable.
The proposition asserts only the stated non-strict error bound; it does not assert that the bound is sharp, that s is unique, or that a nearest representable value exists for every exact real.
